arguments.title: Stop the 60s poll killing playback
arguments.argument:
correctness-1 and offline-1 are true defects, but a repair issue that never fires is a bug no user has ever seen; nobody is filing a ticket about a missing notification. frontend-cards-2 is the one a person feels every time they use the product: `_load()` always ends in `this._render()` (line 499-501), `_render()` assigns `this._card.innerHTML` (line 678), and the open clip is `<video controls autoplay src=...>` (line 622). The 60s `setInterval(() => this._load(), 60000)` (line 441) therefore blows away the player mid-clip and autoplays it from zero. Every clip longer than a minute is unwatchable in the card.

Simplest fix that delivers: skip the re-render in `_load`'s finally while `this._playing` is set. One guard, one sitting, trivially revertible. Falsifiable test in tests/test_cards.mjs, which already drives `_playing` and asserts on `innerHTML` (lines 290-300): set `_playing`, run `_load()`, assert the markup was not rebuilt.

Tradeoff I accept: the list goes stale while you watch. That is the correct priority — you are watching, not browsing.

I open correctness-1, and I can tell you exactly why 1134 tests missed it: repairs.py has no behavioural test at all. Every assertion in tests/test_platforms.py is a substring match against the module's own source. tests/test_platforms.py:120 is literally `self.assertIn("if not total or free is None:", REPAIRS)` — that passes whether the keys are `storage_total` or `storage_totally_wrong`. Line 115 splits source on `def _storage`; line 137 greps coordinator.py text. No test ever calls `async_check`.

That makes correctness-1 the most falsifiable item on the board. The premise is grep-verifiable now: repairs.py:114-115 reads `storage_total`/`storage_free`; status.py:237-238 emits `storage_free_gb`/`storage_total_gb`. The copy-paste source is sensor.py:50, where those are entity keys, not reading keys.

Fix: two key names, plus one test that constructs a fake coordinator with real status.py output and asserts the issue fires. Tradeoff: it does not fix the string-match habit — offline-1 lives in the same blind spot — but it converts one file from text-asserted to called. Same-sitting, trivially revertible. Scope cut: no repairs.py refactor.

arguments.title: Reauth instead of infinite login retry
arguments.argument:
I open the case for ha-conformance-1 (security-1 is the same defect; merge them). I opened `__init__.py`: every connect() failure — including a rejected password — becomes ConfigEntryNotReady, and `config_flow.py` has no `async_step_reauth` at all (steps are user/init/faces/layout/sensitivity/settings), with zero `reauth` keys in en.json or strings.json. So a changed cloud password means HA retries the login on a backoff forever, with no repair card and no way for the user to enter new credentials short of deleting the entry.

Crucially this collides with the hardware constraint the codebase itself already respects: the first-refresh handler warns the hub "wedges under repeated ones and recovers only on a timeout". Auth failure is exactly the case where retrying is both useless and harmful.

Scope: catch the auth-shaped error, raise ConfigEntryAuthFailed, add async_step_reauth_confirm plus two translation keys. One sitting, reversible, and it leaves a falsifiable test — assert ConfigEntryAuthFailed and assert connect() called once. Tradeoff: classifying "auth-shaped" from pytapo's untyped exceptions is the only judgement call; be conservative, default to NotReady.

citations.quote: except Exception as err: ... raise ConfigEntryNotReady(f"Cannot reach the H500 at {entry.data[CONF_HOST]}: {err}") from err
recovers only on a timeout. The exception still leaves, because it is what schedules the retry.
async_step_user / async_step_init / async_step_faces / async_step_layout / async_step_sensitivity / async_step_settings

arguments.argument:
offline-2 is the one defect on this board that the hardware constraint itself makes dangerous, and the tests missed it because it lives in __init__, not in logic.

I opened coordinator.py:835-869 firsthand. The guard is `elapsed >= AUTO_RESTART_COOLDOWN` with `elapsed = now - self._auto_restarted`, and `_auto_restarted` starts at 0.0 with `now = int(dt_util.utcnow().timestamp())` (line 716). After every Home Assistant restart or config-entry reload, elapsed is ~1.8 billion seconds: the six-hour cooldown is vacuously satisfied, and the breaker `0 < elapsed <= CURE_WINDOW` never trips. So a supervisor restarting HA, or an owner toggling options, reboots a wedged hub on the *first* poll, every time — exactly the repeated-reconnect pressure the charter forbids adding. Wall-clock also means a host booting before NTP sync can invert the comparison.

Lazy fix: set `_auto_restarted = utcnow()` at construction (one line, one grace window per HA start), not a Store. Tradeoff: a genuine post-restart wedge waits six hours; that is the safe direction. Falsifiable test: build a coordinator, poll with media_status "wedged", assert reboot was not called.

arguments.title: Bound preview start to known clips
arguments.argument:
I open security-2, and I widen why it matters: this is the integration's only trust boundary, and its whole validation is `if start < 0 or index < 0` (preview.py:55-56). Everything past that goes straight into `client.iter_recording(camera, start_time, start_time + PREVIEW_SECONDS, kind="preview")` (media.py:180-182) — one media session per request, on hardware the charter says wedges under session pressure. So the real need isn't "reject a bad int", it's: a signed-URL replay or a curious authenticated user can walk start_time and mint unbounded sessions plus unbounded `.ts.part` temp files, since the on-disk cache only hits for a start that already produced a frame.

Laziest fix that delivers it: the coordinator already caches clips — check `start` is a known clip start, else 404. One guard, no new state, reversible. Tradeoff: a clip listed after the last poll 404s until the next one; acceptable versus a wedged hub. Leaves the falsifiable test tests-4 says doesn't exist: preview.py's HTTP path has zero coverage today, so any test here is net-new teeth. No new network calls, nothing phones home.

Not proposing rate limiting or a session semaphore — speculative until the guard proves insufficient.

scores.why: I opened the card myself: the 60s setInterval, the finally-block _render, the innerHTML rebuild and the autoplay video element are all exactly as quoted, so the mid-clip reset is a real, user-felt defect with a one-guard fix and a test hook that already exists; debate value is lower because it dismisses rival ideas by assertion rather than engaging their evidence.

Verified firsthand: repairs.py:114-115 reads storage_total/storage_free while status.py:237-238 emits storage_free_gb/storage_total_gb, and the cited tests are genuinely substring matches against module source, so the explanation for why 1134 tests missed it holds; impact is a silent never-firing disk warning rather than a visible break.

Confirmed by grep: no async_step_reauth and no ConfigEntryAuthFailed anywhere in the component or tests, and no reauth translation keys, so a changed password means endless retry against hardware this project documents as wedging under repeated auth; feasibility is docked for the acknowledged judgement call of classifying untyped pytapo exceptions.

The vacuous-cooldown mechanism checks out firsthand — _auto_restarted starts at 0.0 while elapsed is computed from a Unix timestamp, so the six-hour guard is satisfied on the first poll after every restart; impact is held below 8 because the branch also requires reboot is not None, i.e. the owner opted in, which the argument never prices.

The quoted validation and the per-request media session are real, but the load-bearing harm — unbounded session minting by a replayed signed URL or curious user — is asserted rather than shown, with no read of the view's auth posture, and the known-clip-start guard trades a real behavioural regression for a threat whose actor is never pinned down.

open_concerns.concern: The vacuous-cooldown branch only runs when reboot is not None, i.e. the owner opted into automatic restarts. If that option is off by default, the blast radius is a small subset of installs and the impact case shrinks sharply; nobody priced the default.

The preview endpoint's authentication posture is never established. If it is a HomeAssistantView with requires_auth left at its default, the attacker must already be an authenticated HA user, which reprices the whole threat and may make the proposed known-clip-start guard a net regression.

arguments.argument: C3 is resolvable without a pytapo exception classifier, and I opened the file that resolves it. api.py already ships an unauthenticated reachability probe: `sock = socket.create_connection((host, port)...) except OSError: return "unreachable"` (api.py:107-109), with "healthy"/"wedged" for a hub that answers. So the signal is orthogonal to the exception text: connect() failed AND the probe is not "unreachable" means the hub is up and refused us — ConfigEntryAuthFailed. Otherwise keep ConfigEntryNotReady. No new login, no media session, no WAN call; the existing probe is reused, satisfying constraints 1 and 2. Falsifiable test: fake client, connect raises, probe returns "healthy" → expect ConfigEntryAuthFailed; probe "unreachable" → ConfigEntryNotReady. Note config_flow.py:55-56 collapses everything to `errors["base"] = "cannot_connect"` — same laziness, but there the user retypes, so leave it; scope stays __init__.py only. Steelman for frontend-cards-2: it is the only candidate a user feels within one second, and its guard is smaller than mine. It loses only because a restarted video is annoying, while a wedged hub after repeated logins is the hardware failure this repo is built around.

arguments.argument: C3 is answerable, and I answered it by opening pytapo itself. The two failure modes are distinguishable at the type level, not the string level: an unreachable hub surfaces as a `requests.RequestException` propagating out of `transport.send` (pytapo only swallows it in the KLAP probe, `__init__.py:144`), while a rejected session comes back as JSON and is re-raised as a plain `Exception("Error: {msg}, Response: {json}")` at `__init__.py:268-272`. So the classifier is: raise ConfigEntryAuthFailed only when the error is NOT an OSError/RequestException and its text carries an error_code; everything else stays ConfigEntryNotReady. That fails safe toward retry, which kills the C3 regression — a briefly-down hub is never misclassified. It also survives HA restart, since reauth state lives in the config entry, not coordinator memory (unlike offline-2, which I dropped). Note -40401 already retries internally (`:264`), so HA's outer retry multiplies logins against hardware documented to wedge under exactly that. Steelmanning frontend-cards-2: it is the only leader a user *sees* fail, and its guard is three lines with an existing test hook — but a restarted video is an annoyance, an entry that never recovers is an outage.

scores.why: Genuinely novel answer to C3 that sidesteps exception parsing by reusing the existing api.py probe, and both firsthand quotes check out verbatim (api.py:106-123, config_flow.py:55-56); docked because the probe also returns "wedged"/"silent" for a hub that accepted the connection, so the stated rule "not unreachable means it refused us" would raise ConfigEntryAuthFailed on exactly the wedge state C3 warns about.

The shared-base point is true and verified (_player at card.js:620-622 lives in the base class all five cards inherit, and test_cards.mjs:288-294 is a ready harness), and the steelman of correctness-1 is honest; but the card evidence is the same ground held in rounds 1 and 2, the impact case is again asserted rather than shown, and the flagged repeat leaves little new.

Concedes C4 outright and rescopes from a two-key rename to a deletion, with every firsthand citation verified (status.py:220-222, :237-239, test_platforms.py:119-120 really is a substring match that would pass on dead code); impact stays modest because the defect is a warning nobody has observed fire.

The round's sharpest evidence: I opened the bundled pytapo and both quotes are exact -- the -40413 device_confirm path raises the identical "Invalid authentication data" string after MAX_LOGIN_RETRIES, so a string classifier misfires on precisely the wedge shape this repo documents; turning that against its own leader as devil's advocate, then offering a scoped first-attempt-only guard, is a landed attack.

Answers C3 with a type-level rule verified firsthand (pytapo/__init__.py:144 swallows RequestException only in the KLAP probe; :267-272 re-raises JSON errors carrying an error_code), and the rule fails safe toward retry, which is what actually kills the regression C3 describes -- the plain "Invalid authentication data" wedge string slot 3 found carries no error_code and so stays ConfigEntryNotReady.

open_concerns.concern: The probe-based variant recreates the very regression it claims to close: api.py returns "wedged" or "silent" whenever the hub accepts the TCP connection but fails the exchange, so "probe is not unreachable therefore the hub refused our credentials" classifies a wedged H500 -- the documented failure mode -- as an auth failure and stops retrying. Any shipped classifier must treat wedged/silent as not-authenticated-failure, and nobody has stated that.

Nobody has shown storage_used_percent is ever non-None against a real H500. It is computed only when disk() yields both video_total_space and video_free_space; if the hub omits those keys the repair never fires before or after the fix, and the rescoped deletion has zero user-visible effect. A single captured status fixture would settle it.
